questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore different ways of teaching Animal Science.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a English speaking country outside of Europe beside the US. Australia, New Zealand, and Canada were the options. Then I looked into the universities UCPH had aggrements with and choose host university due to the courses available.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When you are on your first semester of your maters degree program, you are recommended to apply as an undergraduate student. My experience tell me that the graduate level would be more suitable. Additionally the host university didn't have the greatest introduction week. They could learn a lot from UCPH on how to do it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I bit difficult because you got "spammed" from the University of Guelph with mails almost daily. They were often autogenerated and didn't consider your specific situation or previous answers.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, just picked up me key from the housing office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You could wish for different halls and residences scattered around campus with different housing styles(rommies, single room, housemates, etc.).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: They had many different meal plans available, including places to use them. Some housing offered a shared kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The host university doesn't provide anything for you. I lived in West Residence and had to buy all kitchen equipment, cutlery, and bedding myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I changed from being a bachelors student to a masters student over the summer. I wanted to take graduate courses but could only choose undergraduate courses before the deadline in early June.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy if you don't have special needs

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They provided guides on their website. They also mailed you if any problems occured.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the classes I wanted but had to fight for it because the courses at the host university usually require you to have taken other previous courses at the host university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Due it your way and then talk/write you out of it. The host university has a coordinator who will help you if problems occur.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took the Undergraduate course in "Genetics of Companion Animals" and it doesn't teach you anything new about breeding or genetics directed towards companion animals. Then I took the course "Digital Technologies in Animal Production" which is just an appetizer for what digitalization can do in animal production. You don't learn how to use the layers behind. My other courses were good, but definitely had a different teaching style than I am used to from UCPH.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 fourth year courses(undergraduate level), one on the same BA level as UCPH and two under the BA level at CPH. I also took 1 graduate course which is similar to a UCPH MA level. Overall, if you are a first year or even first semester student on your master at UCPH, then only take graduate courses even dough coordinators at UCPH doesn't recommend it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very differently. The lectures were very much a alike, except how they didn't have teorethical exercises to test your knowledge in the lectures. Instead you had multiple quizzes or home exercises during the semester which each counted for 3-5% of your final grade. You got judged while learning and I am not a big fan of that system.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Animal Welfare Judging & Evaluation (fourth year undergraduate)
Digital Technologies in Animal Production (fourth year undergraduate)
Genetics of Companion Animals (fourth year undergraduate)
Quantative Genetics and Animal Models (Graduate)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Animal Welfare Judging & Evaluation: You learn how to evaluate welfare due to manegment, reasource, and animal-based measures while taking severity, duration, and impact into account.
Quantative Genetics and Animal Models: It is a hard a theoretical course but you are able to get a great outcome out of it. You learn about different mixed model equations and how to determine breeding values.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The cost of buying equipment for a kitchen and bedding. Furthermore I bought sports equipment in order to attend university sports

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more or less similar to prices in Denmark, especially when tipping is normal practice

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have soooo many social/academic/sport clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can think of. From the juggling student association and the water polo team.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the different fairs and look at what you would like to attend. I attended Badminton every Tuesday and Thursday

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend them to study in the weekdays and take a break in every weekend where you go somewhere with friends for 1 day. It gives you a goal with your studies and makes memories with others(not just for yourself)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: To be honest, Your are in your own little exchange student bubble. you don't mingle with the "natives" and the Western world is very much alike

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nope, you can end up living with them if you are lucky or you can attend clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: tipping. I don't like to tip. Tipping is the same as begging in my mind

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: None in particular actually. They are just Canadians

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. choose West Residence. It is like the Danish "Efterskole" there with all you friends as neighbors.
2. Do something as often as you can with friends or clubs. There is time to study and time to experience.
3. Choose courses you think will challenge you, otherwise you won't take anything academically with you from your stay.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Uber is cheap in Canada, renting a car too, so you can get easy around.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making international friends and connections

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: ajusting to their way of teaching and structure the semester with midterms and so on.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: nope

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
